note: Monday catch-up: most weekend AI sends were about Nvidia's leadership crisis, so the list stays short.

top.title: One compromised MCP server got an agent to misuse its other, trusted tools 78% of the time
top.summary: In security testing of an agent wired to five MCP servers, a single poisoned server hid instructions in its output that the agent then carried into calls to the other servers, succeeding 78.3% of the time. The trial count and success definition weren't published, so treat the number as directional; the fix is mapping which tools can act on which tool's output, scoping credentials narrowly and gating irreversible actions.
top.why: Any PMM workflow that pairs a web-reading or inbox-reading connector with one that can send, publish or write to a system of record has exactly this risk, so it belongs in your guardrail checklist and in the case for orchestrated, auditable agent flows.

top.title: Nearly 90% of senior marketers use AI insights daily, but only 36% usually check them
top.summary: A GWI survey of 1,883 senior marketing and insights staff found eight in ten often see wrong or misleading AI findings, more than half made a big decision on one, and 82% reported a bad outcome such as rework, complaints or lost money. Audience work was the weakest spot, and GWI sells audience data, so it has a stake in the result.
top.why: Gives you a hard number for why PMM workflows need a source-and-date rule for AI-sourced claims before they reach positioning or persona docs, and a quality metric worth tracking alongside time saved.

top.title: Two real Claude workflows: a weekly stats report and a support-inbox digest routed to each team
top.summary: Rundown staff described connecting Claude to their newsletter platform for a scheduled weekly stats report with bot-click filtering, and connecting it to a Gmail support inbox, Slack and scheduled tasks so it groups the week's questions by theme and owning team and drafts one post per team for human review. A monthly pass audits ticket drivers and checks saved replies against what people actually asked.
top.why: The inbox-to-themes-to-team-post pattern maps directly onto PMM signal work (field questions, win/loss notes, CI tips), with the human review step already built in.

try_this.title: Map the trust chain of your most-connected Claude setup
try_this.how: List every connector one of your PMM workflows can call, with its permissions and what it can put into context, then ask Claude to flag pairings where a tool reading untrusted content sits next to a tool that can send, publish or overwrite. Put your first approval gate on the riskiest pairing and narrow that connector to read-only where you can.

workflows.title: Anthropic explains the building blocks of always-on agents
workflows.summary: A guide on agents that run indefinitely, keep context across sessions and act without someone watching, breaking down the primitives behind them and how they fit together.
workflows.why: Useful reference before you turn a scheduled PMM task (signal monitoring, digest building) into something that runs and acts on its own.

governance.title: Coder argues for governing where AI runs instead of which tools people use
governance.summary: A vendor whitepaper says single-tool approvals get routed around and proposes five rules enforced in the runtime environment: keep data in, limit each task to the data it needs, allow only approved models, log every action, and track AI spend by person and team.
governance.why: A clean five-rule frame to bring to Legal, Security and IT when marketing wants to use more than one AI tool.

enablement.title: Sales leaders rate AI research tools nearly twice as useful as AI writing tools
enablement.summary: In HubSpot surveys of 300+ sales leaders, 21% said AI research tools had the biggest positive effect on prospecting versus 12% for AI writing tools, and the top barrier to value was reps using AI as a shortcut instead of a research aid (32%). Demonstrated preparation was the top trait of cold calls that convert.
enablement.why: Supports pitching sales-facing AI assets (account research, competitor context) over drafting tools, and suggests measuring whether reps use them before calls.

landscape.title: Congress moves toward tighter AI chip export rules, with Anthropic backing all three bills
landscape.summary: After the Nvidia leadership scandal, bipartisan leaders say chip-location checks, equipment loophole fixes and congressional oversight of sales could pass via the year-end defense bill, and reporting says remote rental of chips to Chinese customers is also in scope. Anthropic publicly supports the bills and OpenAI is reportedly warming to them.

landscape.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so agents can pay without seeing card numbers
landscape.summary: Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, the wallet lets ChatGPT agents buy things on a user's behalf using tokenized payment details.
landscape.why: Another step toward agents that commit money and actions, which raises the stakes on approval gates in any agent workflow.
